q: How do I calculate the emissions of moving chemicals by road tanker per tonne?
title: Chemical road tanker emissions per tonne
short: Take the diesel for the whole trip, including the empty return a dedicated tanker makes, and multiply by 2.68 kg CO2 per litre. Divide by tonnes delivered. Owned tankers are Scope 1; hired tankers are Scope 3 transport, backed by the transporter's data.
audience: Chemical makers, distributors and tanker fleet operators

p: A dedicated chemical tanker may return empty, since cleaning between products limits backloads. Include the return leg; leaving it out understates each tonne.

ul: Diesel per trip, from fuel slips or the transporter.
Tonnes per load, from weighbridge slips.
Washing or cleaning between loads, if done by you.

p: Tankers you own or lease and run are Scope 1. Hired tankers sit in Scope 3, category 4 or 9 depending on who pays for the freight.

example.title: Worked example: one 600 km delivery (illustrative inputs)
lines: Round trip: 600 km loaded + 600 km empty = 1,200 km at 3.5 km per litre = 342.9 litres
Per tonne delivered: 918.9 / 25 t = 36.8 kg CO2
Per tonne-km, loaded distance: 36.8 / 600 = 0.0613 kg CO2
example.note: Mileage and load are illustrative; use fuel slips, trip sheets and weighbridge records.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and fuel card statements (diesel 2.68 and CNG 2.69 kg CO2, IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 record. Hired transport goes to the Scope 3 evidence trail, and distance or tonne-km estimates are labelled as estimates.
